main_text.p: dicuntur,cum diversę inter se naturę per-mixtio monstra gigneret. Quibus rebus offensus Deus, maximéq; malitia hominum,quæ ultra modum processerat,dele-re penitus humanum genus decreverat. Sed Noë, virum justum, vita innocens de-Gen.7.9. stinatæ exemit sententiæ. Idem admonitusDiluvii. a Domino, diluvium terris imminere,arcam immensæ magnitudinis ex lignis co-texuit:acbitumine illitam impenetrabile aquis reddidit, qua ille cum uxore, ac fi-liis tribus,& totidem nuribus est claufus: volucrum etiam paria, itidemque diversi generis bestiarum,eodem clauftro recep-ta,reliqua omnia diluvio absumpta. Igi-Gen.8.tur Noë, cum jam imbrem destitisse, ac quieto in salo arcam circumferri, intelli-geret, ratus id quod erat, aquas decedere, corvum primum explorandæ rei gratia, eoq; non revertente,(ut ego conjicio,ca-daveribus detéto) emisit columbam:quæ cum confistendi locum non reperiisset, reversa est. Rursu{*} remissa,folium olivæemissa retulit, manifestum indicium, nudari ca-l.q. quod magis cumina arborum. tertio demum emissaprobo. non rediit,unde animadversum aquas de-stitisse.Ita Noë arcam egressus est.id gestu amun-

page.notes: The text runs as one paragraph without indents, and it begins mid-sentence, so it is marked as a continuation. The marginal notes "l.q. quod" and "magis" may be split differently in print; I placed them as one note across lines 24 and 25. The star reference after "Rursu" is copied as printed. "acbitumine" appears to be a missing space in the print and is left as printed. The catchword "amun-" is at the lower right.
